questions.question: Explain three reasons why places at lower latitudes are generally warmer than places at higher latitudes.
questions.expected_answer: First, near the equator the sun's rays strike the ground almost vertically, so energy is concentrated on a small area, while at higher latitudes slanting rays spread the same energy over a larger area. Second, slanting rays pass through more atmosphere, so more energy is absorbed or reflected by gases, dust and cloud before reaching the ground. Third, near the equator day length stays close to twelve hours all year, while at higher latitudes winter days are short, giving cold winters and larger seasonal differences. Together these create the tropical, middle-latitude and polar temperature zones.

questions.question: Compare the temperatures of Mbombela and George and explain the difference, including the role of altitude.
questions.expected_answer: Mbombela, at about 25.5 degrees south, has a January mean of about 24 °C and July about 15 °C, an annual range of 9 °C; George, at about 34 degrees south, has a January mean of about 20 °C and July about 13 °C, a range of 7 °C. Mbombela is about 4 °C warmer in summer and 2 °C warmer in winter because its lower latitude gives more direct, concentrated sunlight through less atmosphere. Mbombela is about 660 m above sea level and George about 200 m, so altitude should make Mbombela cooler; it is warmer despite this, so the latitude effect is stronger than the raw comparison suggests. George's smaller range is partly due to the moderating effect of the nearby sea.

questions.question: Explain how latitude influences the rainfall seasons of Mbombela and George.
questions.expected_answer: Heating near the equator makes air rise, giving rain; air sinks around 20 to 35 degrees, giving dry high-pressure belts; further poleward, cold fronts bring rain. These belts move with the sun. In summer they shift south: moist Indian Ocean air flows over the north and east and convection causes thunderstorms, so Mbombela gets about 770 mm mostly from October to March. In winter they shift north: high pressure brings dry weather to the interior while cold fronts reach the south-west. George, between the systems, gets rain from cold fronts, coastal lows and summer weather, so its roughly 800 mm falls in all months: all-year rainfall.
